picks.showTitle: Nitzotzos: Inspiration to Keep Your Spark Alive with Rav Mordechai Burg
picks.title: Yom Kippur - The 955th Gate
picks.summary: What happens when it feels like the door has closed?Acher hears a Bas Kol say, “Return, wayward children, except for Acher.” Neilah itself is the moment when the gates are closing.And yet Chazal teach us that this is precisely the moment not to give up.In this dhmoy, delivered at Mevaseret Mishmar, Rav Burg explores one of the deepest ideas in teshuvah: that even when everything seems sealed, even when a person feels too far gone, there is still a place beyond despair. Teshuvah reaches all the way to the Kisei HaKavod.Sometimes the gate that seems to be closing is the gate you are meant to kee
picks.reason: Explores deep teshuvah themes about hope and return at Yom Kippur's closing.

Miller is cultivating a model for palliative care organizations around the world, and emphasizing healthcare’s quixotic relationship to the inevitability of death. picks.reason: A Jewish conversation on death, meaning, and care from a palliative care perspective.

picks.title: Yom Kippur: Appreciating and Achieving Greatness
picks.summary:
You put on tefillin. You hold back one piece of lashon hara. You say one tefillah with real kavana. It can feel like such a small thing. But what if the true impact of that mitzvah is far greater than anything you can see? Rabbi Shafier reveals a fascinating picture of how your choices affect not only yourself, but the spiritual worlds beyond you. Discover why even the smallest mitzvah matters more than you realize, why an aveirah carries such weight, and how understanding the true power of your actions can completely change the way you approach Yom Kippur. 
 This podcast has been graciously s
picks.reason: Rabbi Shafier explains the spiritual impact of mitzvot and ethical choices on Yom Kippur.

picks.title: The Shmuz on the Parsha: Ha'azinu
picks.summary:
Is there anything you've done that is simply too big to undo? Any mistake that puts you beyond the reach of teshuvah? In this powerful shmuz, Rabbi Shafier explores the extraordinary story of Elisha ben Avuyah, a man who rose to incredible spiritual heights and then fell almost as far as a person could fall. Yet even for him, the door to teshuvah was never truly closed. Discover the mistake that kept Acher from returning, the astonishing power of teshuvah, and why no matter how far you've fallen, it's never too late to come back. 
 This podcast has been graciously sponsored by JewishPodcasts.f
picks.reason: Explores teshuvah and spiritual failure through the story of Elisha ben Avuyah in Jewish tradition.

picks.title: Teshuvah and the God We Think We Know | Rus Devorah Wallen
picks.summary: A conversation about Teshuvah through the dual lens of clinical attachment theory and Torah sources. We explore why perfect attunement in any relationship is a myth, and how the rupture and repair cycle of Teshuvah is actually what deepens our connections, rather than threatening it. Rus Devorah walks through how our early attachment styles get unconsciously projected onto our relationship with God, and offers concrete practices for moving toward a more secure, honest connection with Hashem during this season of return. Rus Devorah Wallen is the founder and owner of Torah Therapeutics. She is
picks.reason: Explores teshuvah through attachment theory and Torah, focusing on relationship with God.

picks.title: Avinu Malkeinu | Rosh Hashanah II
picks.summary:
"We've tried everything, and we nonetheless fear that it just wasn't enough. Now we are here standing before you with no more plays in the playbook. There's nothing more we can do, and we just hope that you can be satisfied with what we were able to fix and forgive us for the rest. Avinu Malkeinu, show us mercy, answer us, not because we're beyond saving, but because we're trying."

Intro provided by rabbinic intern Jacob Schatz.
picks.reason: A heartfelt Rosh Hashanah prayer reflecting on mercy and human effort in teshuvah.

picks.showTitle: In Such A Time: Conversations on Jewish Life, Leadership & Meaning
picks.title: Ep. 56: Rosh Hashanah Sermon 5787 - Loneliness, Rootedness and the Four P’s

What can the Jewish story teach us about overcoming the personal dislocation so many face today?Listeners are invited on a deeply personal and thought-provoking journey—beginning with a young adult’s search for community in San Francisco and moving through the social science, literature, and enduring wisdom that point us towards connection, purpose, and resilience.Explore the “4 Ps” of meaningfu
picks.reason: Rosh Hashanah sermon addressing loneliness and meaning through Jewish tradition.

picks.title: Chullin 141 and 142 - The End
picks.summary:
On today’s pages, Chullin 141 and 142, we reach the end of Tractate Chullin and look back at what months of studying meat, kashrut, and the intricacies of eating have taught us. Rabbi Dovid Bashevkin joins us to explain why our most basic need for nourishment can become an expression of Jewish identity—and a reminder that we depend on something beyond ourselves. What does keeping kosher ultimately ask us to sanctify? Listen and find out.



Also, celebrate the end of Tractate Chullin with Chullin out, our playlist of every song we referenced along the way.

picks.reason: End of Tractate Chullin study linking kosher laws to Jewish identity and sanctity.

picks.title: Asking Forgiveness Before Yom Kippur
picks.summary: Yom Kippur is a day of atonement and expiation. On this auspicious day, the Almighty forgives us for all our transgressions and we become purified before God. But the purification of Yom Kippur is limited to sins between man and God. For interpersonal transgressions, there is no atonement unless the aggressor appeases and secures forgiveness […]
picks.reason: Jewish teaching on forgiveness and interpersonal atonement before Yom Kippur.

picks.showTitle: Inspiration for the Nation with Yaakov Langer
picks.title: Rebetzin Sara Rigler: She Was a Hindu Nun for 15 Years Until a Rav Asked Her Real Name
picks.summary: Rebbetzin Sara Yocheved Rigler spent 15 years living in an ashram. She meditated three times a day, taught Vedanta & Hindu philosophy, and served as personal secretary to the guru. She went east searching for God.Then one conversation with an Orthodox rabbi turned her whole world upside down. 8 months later, she was studying Torah in Jerusalem.Today she is one of the most widely read Jewish authors alive and a world class Torah teacher. We spoke about those 15 years in the ashram, a life altering (and reincarnation) experience around her fear of having children, and what she found in Judaism t
picks.reason: A Jewish author recounts her spiritual journey from Hinduism to Torah study and Jewish faith.

picks.title: Hullin 139: A Nest on Your Head
picks.summary: Consecrated birds are exempt from the mitzvah of sending away the mother bird -- what is the case? Well, what if a person consecrated the baby birds in the nest? Returning them to the nest if the mother bird returns to them, then there's no requirement to send her away anyway! Maybe he's consecrating the mother bird. Plus, what happens if a consecrated bird escapes to the wild?! Note that the Gemara narrows the mishnah's halakhah to a very specific case, in contrast to the original phrasing. picks.reason: Detailed Talmudic discussion on laws about consecrated birds and related halakhic nuances.

picks.title: Hullin 138: Sending Away the Mother Bird
picks.summary: Finishing the 11th chapter and beginning the 12th chapter. First, how much wool must one give in terms of worth? And how must it be presented? Note the famous proverb about reaching for too much as an unsuccessful project, whereas a less ambitious grasp will be successful. Rabbi Josh Feigelson explores an ancient teaching about directing our hearts toward the Holy of Holies and offers a simple mindfulness practice called The Gentle Knock, a way to pause, reconnect, and come home to ourselves with compassion rather than judgment.
